references.description: Flat join of entity and security: one row per security, plus one row with NULL security_id and symbol for every reporting company that has no security (for example a subsidiary that files only because it issues public debt, or a delisted registrant).  Filter symbol IS NOT NULL for listed securities only.  For any index-membership question, current or historical, join index_membership on cik; this table carries no membership flags because those are snapshot-only and single-index.

status.description: ACTIVE when the registrant has a ticker in SEC's company_tickers.json on the day the data was built, else INACTIVE.  This is a statement about the TICKER FILE, not about whether the company still files with the SEC: it says whether the company is listed today.  Use `is_public` for the classified listed view and `is_active` (on this table `is_entity_active` for `still alive`.  The two can disagree: a non-traded REIT or a debt-only registrant files every quarter but has no ticker (INACTIVE + still filing); a company whose ticker lingers on the list after it stopped filing is ACTIVE + not filing.

is_active.description: The SECURITY's ticker spell is open (security.valid_to IS NULL); NULL on a company with no security.  Says nothing about the registrant: for `still alive` use `is_entity_active`.

is_primary_ticker.description: TRUE for the entity's primary listing.  Multi-share-class issuers (BRK-A/BRK-B, GOOG/GOOGL) have several rows here; filter is_primary_ticker=TRUE for one row per CIK.

is_public.description: TRUE when the registrant is exchange-listed today.  NULL means never classified, not FALSE.  Not the same as `is_active` on this table, which describes the security's ticker spell.

is_entity_active.description: TRUE when the registrant still files with the SEC.  Use it for `still alive`; `status` only says whether the CIK is on SEC's ticker list today, and the two can disagree in both directions (a non-traded REIT is status INACTIVE, is_entity_active TRUE).  NULL means never classified.  Not the same as `is_active` on this table, which describes the security's ticker spell.

succeeded_by_cik.description: The declared corporate-succession link, NULL for almost every row.  When present, the registrant on this row was reorganised into the CIK named here.  A ticker resolver should follow this link instead of guessing succession from which CIK holds more facts.

entity.description: Legal structure and profile of reporting companies.

sic_description.description: Full SEC SIC industry label (e.g. 'Electronic Computers'), the companion to `sic_code`.

status.description: ACTIVE when the registrant has a ticker in SEC's company_tickers.json on the day the data was built, else INACTIVE.  This is a statement about the TICKER FILE, not about whether the company still files with the SEC: it says whether the company is listed today.  Use `is_public` for the classified listed view and `is_active` for `still alive`.  The two can disagree: a non-traded REIT or a debt-only registrant files every quarter but has no ticker (INACTIVE + still filing); a company whose ticker lingers on the list after it stopped filing is ACTIVE + not filing.

state_of_incorporation_description.description: Full SEC label for the state-of-incorporation code (e.g. 'Delaware').

mailing_address.description: Mailing address (separate from HQ) — registered agent / correspondence target.  Often differs from business_address for foreign issuers and trusts.

flags.description: SEC-flagged status string (e.g. 'Shell', 'Delinquent'). NULL for clean issuers.

has_insider_transactions.description: SEC declares Form 4/5 activity exists for this issuer.

is_insider_owner.description: SEC declares this CIK itself owns insider holdings.

is_public.description: TRUE when the registrant's current listing is exchange-listed; FALSE for non-traded or unregistered; NULL when there is no evidence to classify it.

is_active.description: TRUE when the registrant still files with the SEC; FALSE when inactive (deregistered, acquired, dormant); NULL when it was never classified and has no filing.  Independent of `status`, which only says whether the CIK is on SEC's ticker list: a delisted-but-still-filing company is status INACTIVE + is_active TRUE, a ticker that outlived the company is status ACTIVE + is_active FALSE.  Use this column for `still alive / still reporting`, and `status` or `is_public` for `listed today`.

former_names.description: JSON array of {name, from, to} objects: the company's prior names.  Useful for ticker-history queries and merger lineage.  Empty array when the issuer has never renamed.

last_seen_at.description: Data-freshness stamp, not a company fact: the date this row was last refreshed.  After a full refresh every company carries the same date; it says nothing about when the company last filed.  Use MAX(filing.filing_date) for that, and is_active for `still reporting`.

succeeded_by_cik.description: The declared corporate-succession link: NULL for the overwhelmingly common case, else the CIK of the registrant this one was reorganised into (a redomestication, holding-company inversion, or similar new-CIK event).  Only set where the successor restates the predecessor's numbers.  Never a ticker-recycling coincidence (DEC, AMR, ARC).  Also published on `references`.

security.description: Ticker symbols and tradeable instrument metadata (SCD Type 2 with date ranges).

is_primary_ticker.description: TRUE for the entity's primary listing.  Multi-share-class issuers (BRK-A/BRK-B, GOOG/GOOGL) have several active rows; filter is_primary_ticker=TRUE for one row per CIK.

filing.description: Metadata for all SEC filings processed.

superseded_by.description: Accession id of the filing that supersedes this one in the amendment chain; NULL when this is the latest version.

size.description: Filing size in bytes (per SEC submissions feed).

is_xbrl.description: SEC-declared: filing carries an XBRL exhibit.

is_xbrl_numeric.description: TRUE when the XBRL exhibit carries machine-readable numeric facts.  Distinct from is_xbrl and is_inline_xbrl.

primary_document.description: Filename of the lead document in the filing package.

primary_doc_description.description: SEC-provided label describing the primary document.

core_type.description: form_type without the `/A` amendment suffix (e.g. `10-K/A` becomes `10-K`).  Use it for form-family filtering when you do not care whether a filing is the original or an amendment.

film_number.description: SEC EDGAR microfiche / film number assigned at acceptance.

act.description: Securities-Act designator: ``33`` (1933 Act), ``34`` (1934 Act), or empty.  Helps distinguish registration-statement vs. exchange-act filings.

is_audited.description: Filing is an annual (audited) report — TRUE for 10-K / 20-F / 40-F and their amendments, FALSE for 10-Q / 8-K / etc.

fact.description: Standardized financial data points (US-GAAP XBRL mapped to canonical standard_concept labels).

fact_id.description: Stable identifier of this fact.  Cite it to trace a number back to its source filing.

concept.description: The raw XBRL tag as filed (bare local name, e.g. 'Revenues').  Look it up in `taxonomy_guide`.

standard_concept.description: The standardized concept name (e.g. 'Revenue'); 'Other' when the tag is not mapped.  Look it up in the `standard_concept` table.

priority.description: Primary-row flag.  Within each filing, 1 marks the one row chosen for each fact (entity, standard_concept, period_end, unit, duration); 0 marks sibling tags that map to the same standard concept.  Filter `priority = 1` for one row per fact per filing.

value.description: Raw as-reported value string, before numeric parsing.  Holds text for non-numeric facts (e.g. cover-page strings); for numeric facts use `numeric_value`.

numeric_value.description: The value as reported in this specific filing (accession_id).

fiscal_year.description: Fiscal year the fact's `period_end` belongs to, based on the company's own fiscal-year end.  A comparative figure in a later 10-K keeps its own period's year.  Group by `period_end` when exactness matters.

accuracy_score.description: Legacy 0-1 score of how well the reported tag matched the standardized concept.  Superseded for filtering by `confidence_score`; kept for traceability.

confidence_score.description: Per-fact confidence in [0, 1].  It only goes down for evidence we can point at, never from opinion.  Read it as: 0.95 or higher means we hold no evidence against the fact (the normal case, about 99.9% of rows, across all years); about 0.80 means a later filing revised it (see the restatement diff on /radar); below 0.60 means an accounting identity failed on its filing.  The inputs (`identity_violation_count`, `restatement_count`, `is_audited`) ship in this table so you can check it.  There is no age term: an older filing is not less trustworthy, so `>= 0.95` is not a recency filter.

reliability_code.description: Nominal reliability bucket (1-4): 1 = preliminary (identity errors present), 2 = announced (clean, unaudited), 3 = audited (audited and clean), 4 = restated (audited, clean, multiple versions on file).  NOT an ordinal: 4 is not 'better' than 3, so `WHERE reliability_code >= 3` silently includes restated facts.  To rank by quality, order by `confidence_score`; use this column only for equality tests against one bucket.

identity_violation_count.description: Number of error-severity accounting-identity checks that failed on this fact's filing.

restatement_count.description: Number of times this fact was re-reported in later filings.  0 = never restated; N = restated N times.  Counted per raw filer tag and reporting period (period_start, period_end, unit), not per standard concept and not per fiscal_period label; grouping by either would invent restatements.

is_estimated.description: TRUE when part of the published value was inferred rather than read directly from the source.  In practice this is a monetary scale on pre-2001 filings, or a share count / EPS whose units were visibly mis-typed by the filer.  Such facts carry a confidence_score deduction.  Where a scale could not be established, the monetary fact is not published at all.  FALSE on ordinary XBRL facts.

data_quality.description: How this number was obtained.  'standard' = read from an XBRL exhibit the filer tagged (2009 onward; the overwhelming majority of rows).  'ex27_fds' = parsed from an EX-27 Financial Data Schedule, the filer's own machine-readable summary required on 10-Ks and 10-Qs from 1994 to 2000.  'html_derived' = extracted from the filing's rendered financial statements (2001-2008, where no machine-readable exhibit exists).  'sgml_derived' = extracted from the plain-text statements of a pre-2003 filing.  'human_verified' = a value a reviewer read off the filing by hand and recorded with a link to the evidence; it is never estimated and ships at confidence 1.0.  'period_after_filing' = a statement or cover-page fact whose period ends more than a day after the filing was accepted, usually a date the filer mistyped; the value is kept, and `data_quality = 'standard'` excludes it.  'equity_bridge' = an equity figure derived from the same filing's own balance sheet for the same date rather than read from a tag; it only fills a gap, and `label` carries the proof.  'equity_corrected' = the filer's equity tags contradicted each other and one reading makes the balance sheet foot; the filer's own row is kept beside it.  'eps_bridge' = total EPS copied from the same filing's continuing-operations EPS where the filing reports no total EPS and discontinued operations are zero.  'fallback_bridge' = a headline line (net income, operating cash flow, total revenue, capex, cash) built from the same filing's own component lines where the filing reports no headline line; it only fills a gap.  'bank_revenue_gross' = a bank's gross revenue (interest and dividend income plus noninterest income), the usual vendor convention for depository institutions; it is used in preference to the filer's net revenue tag for banks.  Filter on this column to restrict a backtest to XBRL-era facts; `confidence_score` already carries a deduction for the non-XBRL sources, and the raw source tag stays in `concept`.

accounting_standard.description: Reporting taxonomy of the source filing: 'US-GAAP' or 'IFRS'.  Usually 'IFRS' for 20-F / 40-F foreign issuers.

reporting_currency.description: ISO-4217 currency code when the unit is monetary (e.g. 'USD', 'EUR', 'JPY').  NULL for non-monetary facts (shares, ratios, days).

derivation_type.description: How a value was derived rather than read.  Quarterly flows: 'standalone', 'ytd_subtraction', 'not_applicable'.  Equity bridge rows: 'equity_e1' to 'equity_e4' and 'equity_temp_e4' (the balance-sheet equation that was solved), 'equity_zero_*' (a zero the filing proves), 'equity_sign_fix' / 'equity_total_fix' (a balance-sheet correction), 'equity_nci_sum' (noncontrolling interest rebuilt from its component lines).  'preferred_par_only' marks the filer's own PreferredEquity row whose value is only par, not the carrying amount.  'eps_continuing_ops' = total EPS copied from continuing-operations EPS.

value_current.description: The latest-known value for this (entity_id, standard_concept, period_end, unit): what an analyst looking today would see.

value_as_filed.description: The originally reported value: the first one accepted for this fact.

first_filed_at.description: Timestamp of the first disclosure of this fact (earliest acceptance time).

restated.description: TRUE if any version of this fact differs from the others, meaning a later filing restated the number.  WARNING: this is computed against all filings to date, NOT point-in-time: a query as of a past date may still see TRUE for a restatement that happened after that date.  For point-in-time work, use the MCP field `lineage.restated_in_warehouse` and treat this flag as informational.

filing_registrant.description: Every registrant of an SEC accession.  ``filing`` has ONE row per ``accession_id``, owned by the first registrant, so a combined (co-registrant) filing appears under only one CIK there; ``fact.entity_id`` still names each registrant.  Join this table to ``filing`` on ``accession_id`` to list a company's filings including the combined ones: ``SELECT f.* FROM filing f JOIN filing_registrant r ON r.accession_id = f.accession_id WHERE r.entity_id = :cik``.  A registrant that filed no numeric fact under its own CIK may be absent.

entity_id.description: One registrant of the accession (10-digit CIK).

index_membership.description: Index constituents keyed on `cik`.  Join `references.cik = index_membership.cik` to attach company metadata (name, sector, ticker).  Filter by `index_name` for the index, and by `effective_date` / `removal_date` for the as-of window (half-open [) semantics).  `cik` is named `cik` here, not `entity_id` as on security, filing and fact.  HISTORICAL DEPTH AND PROVENANCE DIFFER BY INDEX.  Read this before using the table for point-in-time work.  The `source`, `confidence` and `date_precision` columns say how far to trust each row's dates. * SP500: from 1996-01-02.  Membership comes from SEC portfolio filings of index funds (N-PORT and N-CSR) and, for change dates, issuers' 8-Ks, Form 25 / Form 15 and public reports of index changes, plus publicly available constituent lists.  There are about 500 members at every year end from 1996.  Where a change date is not known to the day, the row is a window: `effective_date` is the conservative point (the latest plausible join day, the earliest plausible exit day) and the bounds sit in the `*_earliest` / `*_latest` columns.  Most changes before 2007 are windows.  A change newer than the latest fund filing is `status='provisional'` until a fund filing confirms it, which can take a few months.  Rows with `date_precision` NULL come from an earlier, coarser build; it under-counts the index before about 2006, so grade those rows by `confidence`. * RUSSELL1000 / RUSSELL2000 / RUSSELL3000: from 2000-09-30, `medium` confidence, `source='fund_holdings'`.  Derived from public SEC portfolio filings of funds tracking each index.  Carry these bounds into any conclusion drawn from the Russell rows.  (1) Observation spacing varies: roughly one to four observations a year from 2000 through 2006, monthly from 2007 on, so a join or leave date is only as precise as the interval between observations and is never exact to the day in the early years.  (2) A tracking fund only proxies its index: a few holdings sit outside it and a sampled fund can miss members, so these rows are our derived membership, not the index itself.  (3) There is no Russell data before 2000-09-30; an earlier date returns zero rows because we do not carry it, which does not mean the index was empty.  Confidence is therefore `medium` and never `high`, which leaves the MCP `pit_safe` flag false.  KNOWN GAP: no Russell observation exists between 2016-12-30 and 2017-07-31.  Departures in that period collapse onto 2016-12-31 and arrivals onto 2017-07-31, so the June 2017 reconstitution appears to happen on 31 July, and a year-end 2016 query returns about 2,600 RUSSELL3000 members rather than about 2,900.  SP500 is unaffected.  Index membership is reconstructed independently by Valuein from public information: SEC filings (index funds' N-PORT, N-CSR, N-30D and N-Q schedules; issuers' 8-Ks, Form 25 / 15, 8-K12B), publicly available constituent lists and public reports of index changes; never from an index provider's licensed constituent data. Index names are trademarks of their owners; Valuein is not affiliated with or endorsed by any index provider.

index_name.description: Short code.  Exactly four values: SP500, RUSSELL1000, RUSSELL2000, RUSSELL3000.  Depth and provenance differ per index; see the table description.

effective_date.description: First trading day the company traded as a member (the day the change took effect, not the announcement date) when that day is known (`date_precision` 'day').  When it is not, a conservative point estimate: the latest plausible join day, so a company is never shown as a member before it could have joined.  The bracket is `effective_date_earliest` / `effective_date_latest`.  On rows with `date_precision` NULL, a confidence below 'high' means the day may be approximate.

removal_date.description: First trading day the company was NOT a member.  NULL = current member.  [) interval: a company removed on 2017-06-19 is NOT a member on 2017-06-19.

removal_reason.description: merger | acquisition | bankruptcy | criteria | spinoff | reorganization | other.  reorganization: the company moved to a new SEC registrant (holding company, redomicile, inversion) and `successor_cik` took the seat on the same day.  NULL when removal_date IS NULL.

successor_cik.description: Acquirer CIK when removal_reason is merger or acquisition; the new registrant when it is reorganization.  Essential for backtests crossing M&A: without it, a stock disappearing looks like a delisting.

source.description: What fixed the row's dates: `public_list` (a public constituent list stated the day), `fund_filings` (only bracketed by two fund portfolio filings, so a date window), `event_filing` (dated by the issuer's or exchange's own filing, such as Form 25, Form 15 or an 8-K), `rule_calendar` (the quarterly rebalance date), `succession_config` (a declared predecessor to successor registrant), `fund_holdings` (publicly disclosed fund portfolio holdings, Russell rows, always confidence 'medium'), `manual`.  Rows from the earlier SP500 build carry `historical_seed` or `public_constituent_list`.

confidence.description: high | medium | low.  `high` = day-level dates (or an open end) that are well corroborated; `medium` = a date window up to about a quarter, thin corroboration, or `status='provisional'`; `low` = a longer window or a single observation.  Rows from the earlier SP500 build are graded by how certain their source is, `low` for most pre-2001 dates.  Russell rows are always `medium`.  The MCP `pit_safe` flag is true only when every matched row is `high`.

notes.description: Always NULL; kept so existing readers do not break.

first_seen_date.description: The first date this constituent was observed in a source portfolio filing.  NULL on rows that come from curated lists rather than observed portfolios.  For a Russell row this is the honest observation window: `effective_date` may precede it only by the observation spacing.

last_seen_date.description: The last date this constituent was observed in a source portfolio filing.  Populated wherever `first_seen_date` is.

avg_weight_pct.description: Average weight (%) of the company in the index over the observed window.  NULL where weights are not available.

effective_date_earliest.description: Earliest plausible join day.  Equal to `effective_date` when `date_precision` is 'day'; NULL when the company was already a member at the start of our data and on rows with `date_precision` NULL.

effective_date_latest.description: Latest plausible join day.  For a window row `effective_date` is this bound (conservative); for a filing-anchored window it is the stated day.  NULL on rows with `date_precision` NULL.

removal_date_earliest.description: Earliest plausible first day NOT a member.  For a window row `removal_date` is this bound (conservative).  NULL while a member and on rows with `date_precision` NULL.

removal_date_latest.description: Latest plausible first day NOT a member.  NULL while a member and on rows with `date_precision` NULL.

date_precision.description: day | window | NULL.  'day' when each dated end is a single known day; 'window' when the change is only bounded (including ends anchored on a filing-stated event such as a trading stop, closing, Form 25 / 15 or succession, and rows starting at the start of our data).  NULL = a row from the earlier SP500 build or a Russell row, not graded.

status.description: confirmed | provisional | NULL.  'provisional' = the change is known from a public source but no fund filing confirms it yet; it is included in current-members queries, and a point-in-time query that matches it is not `pit_safe`.  NULL on rows with `date_precision` NULL.

industry_classification.description: Point-in-time industry classification (SEC SIC): one row per company and SIC spell, from the SIC each filer itself reported in its own filings.  `valid_from` is the acceptance instant of the first filing that showed the SIC; `valid_to` (exclusive) is where the next spell starts, NULL for the current one.  There are no rows before a company's first evidence: history is never invented, so a backtest dated earlier must decide for itself (using the first spell is the nearest-in-time choice).  A -> B -> A is three spells; a real reassignment is not smoothed.  `references.sector` / `industry` / `sic_code` and `entity` are current values and are NOT point-in-time: use this table for as-of questions (`valid_from <= t AND (valid_to IS NULL OR t < valid_to)`).  `sector` uses the same SIC-to-sector mapping as `references.sector`.  No GICS (licensed): 4-digit SIC is the finest level published.  Sliced like `references`, no date window.

sic_description.description: SEC's published description of the code; the latest filer-reported text when the code is not on the SEC list.

sector.description: Sector of this SIC under the same mapping as references.sector.

industry.description: Filer-reported SIC description (the meaning of entity.industry).

valid_from.description: Acceptance instant (UTC) of the first filing showing this SIC.  Every published acceptance timestamp is UTC.

valid_to.description: Exclusive end: the next spell's valid_from; NULL = current.

first_accession_id.description: SEC accession number of the first evidence filing in the spell (NULL if only observed).  Provenance, not a foreign key: it may name a form the filing table does not carry.

last_accession_id.description: SEC accession number of the last evidence filing in the spell (NULL if only observed).  Provenance, not a foreign key: it may name a form the filing table does not carry.

evidence_count.description: Evidence rows folded into the spell.

valid_from_basis.description: sec_acceptance (exact acceptance time) | filing_date_eod (filing date, end of day) | observed (date we saw it).

standard_concept.description: The standardized concept catalog: the dictionary for the `fact.standard_concept` column.  Each row is one concept (Revenue, GrossProfit, LongTermDebt, ...) with its statement, category, definition, default unit and Bloomberg / FactSet field equivalents.  Distinct from `taxonomy_guide` (the raw SEC us-gaap tag reference for `fact.concept`).  Join `fact.standard_concept = standard_concept.standard_concept` for the label.  The 'Other' catch-all row is included.

level.description: L1 (top statement line) | L2 (sector-pack sub-line) | -- (the 'Other' catch-all).

statement_type.description: income | balance_sheet | cash_flow | comprehensive_income | supplemental | dei | notes | other.

category.description: Finer grouping within the statement (e.g. revenue, working_capital, equity).

unit_default.description: Canonical unit (USD | USD/share | shares | pct | …); NULL for non-numeric.

is_flow.description: TRUE for flow (period) measures, FALSE for stock (point-in-time) measures.

parent_concept.description: Parent in the L1→L2 hierarchy (NULL for L1 / 'Other').

sector_pack.description: Sector pack a L2 concept belongs to (banking, insurance, reit, …); NULL unless level='L2'.

bloomberg_equivalent.description: Closest Bloomberg field mnemonic, when one exists.

factset_equivalent.description: Closest FactSet field, when one exists.

gaap_ifrs_comparable.description: TRUE when the concept maps cleanly across US-GAAP and IFRS filers.

reviewed.description: TRUE = an accountant has verified this concept's name, statement_type and definition.  Catalog rows default TRUE; provisional rows are FALSE.

reviewed_by.description: Who signed off (e.g. 'J. Smith, CPA'); NULL when not individually attributed.

reviewed_at.description: ISO date of the CPA sign-off; NULL when not individually attributed.

review_confidence.description: Concept-level trust score in [0, 1].  1.0 = accountant-verified (reviewed = TRUE); lower = provisional, pending review.  Filter `review_confidence >= 1.0` for the verified concept set.  Distinct from per-fact `confidence_score`.

taxonomy_guide.description: SEC us-gaap taxonomy tag reference, one row per raw tag: the dictionary for `fact.concept`, joined on `fact.concept = taxonomy_guide.standard_concept`.  Not the dictionary for `fact.standard_concept`; that is the `standard_concept` table.

level.description: Not populated (always NULL) for the raw us-gaap tag reference; the L1/L2 tier lives in the ``standard_concept`` table.

statement_type.description: Not populated (NULL) for the raw us-gaap tag reference; statement placement lives in the ``standard_concept`` table.

is_active.description: Always TRUE today: rows from earlier taxonomy vintages are kept, not deactivated.

gaap_ifrs_comparable.description: Reserved; not populated by any writer (always FALSE).

ratio.description: Financial ratios per company per fiscal period, derived from fact data.  Point-in-time: each row's `accepted_at` is the SEC acceptance time of the latest input fact, so a restated period is a new vintage row rather than an overwrite.  Filter `accepted_at <= as_of` and take the latest vintage to avoid look-ahead bias.  No accession_id (a ratio can draw on several filings).  `accepted_at` is NULL for cross-sectional rank rows (`*_sector_pctile`) and for years whose source facts carry no acceptance timestamp.  Equity ratios name the equity they use: `return_on_equity` is on common equity (the default basis), `return_on_parent_equity` on parent equity, `return_on_total_equity` on total equity including noncontrolling interest; `book_value_per_share` and the tangible variants are on common equity; `debt_to_equity`, `liabilities_to_equity`, `long_term_debt_to_equity`, `debt_to_capital` and `equity_multiplier` are on total equity.  Averages use the same equity concept at both ends; a missing or non-positive equity leaves the ratio absent.

category.description: Groups ratios for filtering.  Values: profitability | per_share | liquidity | leverage | efficiency | forensic | growth | owner_earnings | valuation.  `valuation` holds only parameter-free measures built from filings: graham_number and ncav_per_share.  The price-based multiples (price-to-earnings, price-to-book, price-to-sales, EV multiples, dividend yield, market cap) were withdrawn on 2026-11-11 and are not published; no share-price series is published.  It carries no intrinsic-value estimate: that depends on the caller's own assumptions, so it is computed on demand (MCP `compute_dcf`) and never published as a fact.

confidence_score.description: Data quality of the period: the average `fact.confidence_score` of the facts feeding it.  Filter >= 0.95 for the cleanest rows.  NULL for cross-sectional rank rows.

fiscal_period.description: FY | Q1 | Q2 | Q3 | Q4 | TTM

accepted_at.description: Point-in-time vintage: the SEC acceptance time of the latest input fact, i.e. when this ratio first became knowable.  NULL for cross-sectional rank rows and un-timestamped years.  Filter `accepted_at <= as_of` for look-ahead-free backtests.

ingested_at.description: Load timestamp; use `computed_at` for ratio freshness.

restatement_events.description: Restatement Radar feed: one row per financial fact that a later filing materially changed from the originally reported value, across the full 1993-to-present archive.  Each row carries the original ('as reported') value, the current ('restated') value, the signed delta, a severity bucket, both filings' accessions for one-click SEC lineage, and a per-company rank of the revision.  Served to all tiers in full, including the free tier, so the public /radar surface always shows the complete feed.  `event_id` is stable across re-restatements, so a /radar/[id] URL does not change.

event_id.description: Stable identifier of the restated fact.  A fact restated twice keeps one id.

concept.description: The raw XBRL tag both filings used (e.g. 'Revenues').  Comparing the same tag in both filings is what makes the diff like-for-like: a reader can open both accessions and confirm the same tag carries two different numbers.

concept_label.description: As-reported label from the latest filing; falls back to standard_concept.

statement_type.description: income_statement | balance_sheet | cash_flow (from the latest vintage).

period_start.description: Start of the reporting window the restated fact covers.  Together with `period_end` it identifies the fact: a 3-month quarter and a 6-month year-to-date figure share a `period_end` but never a `period_start`.  NULL for instant (balance-sheet) facts, which have no duration.

period_end.description: End of the reporting period the restated fact covers.

fiscal_period.description: FY | Q1 | Q2 | Q3 | Q4: a display label carried from the latest filing.  It can be missing or inconsistent across filings, so use `period_start` / `period_end` for identity and this column only to render.

delta_pct.description: Signed relative change: (current − first) / |first|. Positive = revised up.

version_count.description: Number of filings that reported this fact (2 or more for a restatement).

last_filed_at.description: accepted_at of the restating filing: the event's detection time and the feed ordering key.

restated_in_form.description: SEC form the restating filing arrived in (10-K, 10-K/A, 10-Q, 10-Q/A, 20-F, ...).  The most important qualifier on an event: a 10-K/A is the company formally telling the SEC it got a number wrong, while a routine next-year 10-K carrying a revised comparative is a re-file.  Nullable when the filing record is unknown.

restated_in_amendment.description: TRUE when the restating filing is an amendment.  The strongest signal that a restatement is real and acknowledged.  FALSE when unknown; an amendment is never claimed without proof.

first_primary_doc.description: Primary document of the as-reported filing (e.g. 'goog-20251231.htm').  Lets a consumer build SEC's inline-XBRL viewer URL (/ix?doc=/Archives/edgar/data/{cik}/{accn}/{doc}).  NULL when the filing record is unknown; link to the filing index page instead.

current_primary_doc.description: Primary document of the restating filing.  See `first_primary_doc`.

first_is_inline_xbrl.description: TRUE when the as-reported filing is Inline XBRL.  TRUE: link SEC's viewer (https://www.sec.gov/ix?doc=/Archives/edgar/data/{cik}/{accn}/{doc}).  FALSE: link the document directly (/Archives/edgar/data/{cik}/{accn}/{doc}), or {accession}-index.htm when `first_primary_doc` is NULL; the viewer renders nothing for a non-iXBRL document.  FALSE when the filing record is unknown.

current_is_inline_xbrl.description: TRUE when the restating filing is Inline XBRL.  Same link rules as `first_is_inline_xbrl`, applied to `current_accession` / `current_primary_doc`.

disclosure_class.description: How the company told the market: 'non_reliance' | 'amended' | 'undisclosed'.  'non_reliance': an 8-K Item 4.02 ('Non-Reliance on Previously Issued Financial Statements') was filed between the original and the restating filing, the company formally telling the SEC not to rely on what it had reported.  The loudest signal in US disclosure, and rare.  'amended': corrected in a 10-K/A or 10-Q/A.  'undisclosed': the value changed inside a routine periodic filing, with no Item 4.02 and no amendment.  This describes the filing chain, not the filer's intent.  Never NULL: 'undisclosed' is the default.

severity.description: Magnitude bucket of the change: high | medium | low, by size of the relative change.

concept_importance.description: How much an analyst cares that this line moved: 1 headline (revenue, net income, EPS, total assets, operating cash flow), 2 primary statement line, 3 footnote.  Drives `company_rank`.

company_rank.description: Rank of this event within the company's restatement history (1 = most significant), ordered by `concept_importance` first, then size of change, then period.  The feed keeps each company's top 10 events.

insider_party.description: Directory of every insider or reporting person referenced by Form 3/4/5/144.  Keyed on CIK when SEC-registered, otherwise on a normalized name.  Joined to insider_transaction via insider_party_id.  Institutional (full) tier only.

cik.description: 10-digit zero-padded SEC CIK; NULL for filers without an SEC-registered identity (rare individual reporters).

normalized_name.description: Uppercased, whitespace-collapsed name, used to match filers that have no CIK.

insider_filing.description: Form 3 / 4 / 5 / SC 13D / SC 13G / 144 (and amendments): the insider-disclosure filing record, kept apart from `filing` (financial-statement forms).  `subject_cik` is the issuer the disclosure is about, a soft reference (LEFT JOIN to entity.cik; may be NULL or unmatched for foreign, pre-IPO or delisted issuers).  `filer_party_id` links to `insider_party` (the insider or holder).  `insider_transaction` and `insider_ownership` link to this table via accession_id.  Institutional (full) tier only.

accession_id.description: Unique SEC accession ID for this disclosure filing.

subject_cik.description: Issuer CIK the disclosure is about — soft reference (LEFT JOIN to entity.cik; no hard FK).

filer_party_id.description: FK to the insider / holder in insider_party (NULL when unresolved).

filer_cik.description: Denormalised filer CIK for query convenience.

superseded_by.description: Accession of the amendment (3/A, 4/A, 5/A, 144/A, SC 13D/G) that replaces this filing; NULL on the latest version, and NULL where an amendment cannot be matched to exactly one original.  Drop superseded filings (and their insider_transaction rows) with `superseded_by IS NULL` to avoid counting a corrected trade twice.  See `insider_ownership.superseded_by` for 13D/G positions.

accepted_at_precision.description: 'exact' | 'date_only'.  'date_only' means accepted_at is 22:00 America/New_York of filing_date, an upper bound.

accepted_at_source.description: Where accepted_at came from: the filing's own header or SEC submissions data (exact), or the filing date (date_only).

source_format.description: Format the row was read from: xml | dataset | html | text.  NULL on older rows.

original_filing_date.description: Forms 3/4/5 /A: dateOfOriginalSubmission, the filing date of the amended filing.

amends_accession_id.description: Explicit pointer filed by the amendment (Form 144/A and SC 13D/G XML previousAccessionNumber). Soft reference: the amended filing may not be in this table.

is_rule_10b5_1.description: Form 4/5 Rule 10b5-1 checkbox (schema 2023-04+).  NULL = the form version has no checkbox.

plan_adoption_date.description: Form 144 planAdoptionDates.  NULL = none filed, or several distinct dates.

superseded_at.description: The accepted_at of the superseding filing: the instant this filing stops being current.  NULL while it is the latest version.  Filter `superseded_at IS NULL OR superseded_at > :as_of` for a point-in-time view.

insider_transaction.description: Form 3 / 4 / 5 / 144 line items — each row is one transaction, initial holding, or proposed sale by an insider.  transaction_type is 'transaction' (Form 4/5), 'initial_holding' (Form 3), or 'proposed_sale' (Form 144).  Joins to ``insider_filing`` via accession_id, to ``entity`` (issuer) via entity_id (soft ref), and to ``insider_party`` via insider_party_id.  FULL bucket only.

entity_id.description: Issuer CIK (the company whose securities the insider holds).  Soft reference — LEFT JOIN to entity.cik when the issuer is in the fundamentals universe; may not resolve for foreign / pre-IPO / delisted issuers.

transaction_type.description: transaction | initial_holding | proposed_sale.  Flow aggregates use transaction_type = 'transaction'.

price_per_share.description: Price per share as filed, in dollars.  NULL when the filed value is implausible because an aggregate dollar amount was typed into the per-share field; shares and the filing itself are unchanged, so the dollar total stays derivable from the filing.

aggregate_market_value.description: Form 144 only — proposed-sale total dollar value.

accepted_at.description: The parent filing's SEC acceptance instant (UTC), joined from insider_filing at export.

insider_name.description: Reporting insider's name, copied from insider_party for convenience.  NULL if there is no match.

insider_cik.description: Reporting insider's CIK, copied from insider_party (see insider_name).

acquired_disposed_code.description: A | D as filed (transactionAcquiredDisposedCode): the only unambiguous sign for codes J/G/M/C/X.  NULL on holdings, Form 3 and Form 144 rows.

conversion_or_exercise_price.description: Table II derivative conversion or exercise price as filed.  NULL when the box holds only a footnote reference.

exercise_date.description: Table II date exercisable.  NULL when footnote-only.

expiration_date.description: Table II expiration date.  NULL when footnote-only.

footnote_refs.description: Footnote references of this line, one '<column>:<footnote_id>' token each ('price_per_share:F1', 'row:F3').  Resolve against insider_footnote.  NULL = none.

accepted_at_precision.description: From the parent filing: 'exact' | 'date_only' (accepted_at is then 22:00 America/New_York of the filing date, an upper bound).

is_amendment.description: DERIVED: the parent filing is a /A.

superseded_by.description: DERIVED: accession of the amendment that replaces this row's filing; NULL when current.

superseded_at.description: DERIVED: the accepted_at of the superseding filing.  A row is current as of D when accepted_at <= D AND (superseded_at IS NULL OR superseded_at > D).

is_rule_10b5_1.description: DERIVED from the parent filing's Rule 10b5-1 checkbox (Forms 4/5, 2023-04+).

institutional_filing.description: Form 13F-HR / 13F-NT (and amendments) — the manager-rooted filing record.  Distinct from ``filing`` (issuer-rooted) because 13F filings have no single subject issuer (the manager reports a portfolio across many issuers).  FK to ``insider_party`` for the manager.  FULL bucket only — enterprise tier.

accession_id.description: Unique SEC accession ID for this 13F filing.

filer_party_id.description: FK to the manager's row in insider_party.

filer_cik.description: Denormalised manager CIK — mirrors institutional_holding.filer_cik for query convenience.

amendment_no.description: The cover page's amendment number (0 on an original).

superseded_by.description: Accession of the 13F-HR/A RESTATEMENT that replaces this filing (the first restatement filed after it for the same manager and period); NULL on the latest version.  A NEW HOLDINGS amendment only adds positions: it supersedes nothing and stays live beside its original.  A manager's book for a period is the holdings of the filings with ``superseded_by IS NULL`` (summing every filing double counts a restated report).

accepted_at_source.description: Where accepted_at came from: the filing's own header or SEC submissions data (exact), or the filing date (date_only).

source_format.description: Format the row was read from: xml | dataset | text.  NULL on older rows.

report_type.description: 13F HOLDINGS REPORT | 13F NOTICE | 13F COMBINATION REPORT (cover page).

amendment_type.description: RESTATEMENT | NEW HOLDINGS on an amendment; NULL on an original or when unreadable.

table_entry_total.description: Summary page: number of information-table entries.

value_total_usd.description: Summary page: value total, in WHOLE dollars (scaled by value_units like institutional_holding.market_value_usd).

value_units.description: Units of every VALUE in this filing as filed: thousands | dollars.  Published holding values are scaled to whole dollars from this.  NULL on a notice (13F-NT) and on filings not yet classified.

filer_crd_number.description: The manager's FINRA/IARD CRD number (1-12 digits), as filed on the 13F cover.  Joins to investment_adviser.crd_number (Form ADV, also FULL tier) to link a 13F manager to its adviser record.  NULL when not stated.  A public registration number, not a security identifier.

form13f_file_number.description: The manager's Form 13F file number (028-NNNNN), as filed.  NULL when not stated.

reconciliation_status.description: Text-era filings: reconciled | unreconciled | no_totals (whether the filing's own totals check out).  Holdings rows are published only for reconciled filings.

superseded_at.description: DERIVED: the accepted_at of the superseded_by filing; NULL while current.

institutional_holding.description: Form 13F-HR holdings: institutional managers' quarterly position disclosures.  One row per filed information-table line (`holding_line_no`): a filing may list one security on several lines (per investment discretion or other manager), and the position is their sum.  `shares_or_principal_type = 'PRN'` rows are bonds or convertible notes whose `shares` is a face amount in dollars: filter `shares_or_principal_type = 'SH'` before summing shares.  Joins to `institutional_filing` via accession_id; `filer_cik` is the manager CIK.  `subject_entity_id` is the issuer CIK (NULL when the security could not be matched to a company).  Institutional (full) tier only.

filer_cik.description: Manager CIK (same as institutional_filing.filer_cik).  This does NOT resolve against `entity` for most filers: a 13F filer is a money manager, not an SEC-registered company issuer.  Manager identity (name, cik) lives in `insider_party` (`party_type='entity'`; join on `insider_party.cik = institutional_holding.filer_cik`).  A filer_cik with no match in `entity` is expected, not a data-quality defect.

filer_name.description: 13F manager name, copied from insider_party.  NULL only when the manager CIK is unresolved.

share_class_figi.description: Share-class FIGI (12 characters, e.g. BBG001S5N8V8) of the security held; joins to `references.share_class_figi` and `security.share_class_figi`.  Valuein does not publish the CUSIP.  NULL when the security has no share-class FIGI (debt, munis, notes) or when the security cannot be identified; coverage is lower on older rows.  Option rows carry the underlying security's FIGI; `put_call` disambiguates.

subject_entity_id.description: Issuer CIK of the security held.  A genuine share of NULLs is expected: options and derivatives, ETFs and funds of funds, and foreign issuers outside the `entity` universe have no company CIK to resolve to.  Do not read NULL as missing data.

market_value_usd.description: Position value in whole US dollars.  Filers reported 13F VALUE in thousands of dollars before 2023-01-03 (and a minority for months after); published values are scaled so this column is always whole dollars.

put_call.description: PUT | CALL | NULL (NULL = common stock, not an option).

investment_discretion.description: SOLE | DFND | OTR (Form 13F bulk vocabulary) or SOLE | SHARED | NONE (per-filing XML vocabulary).

accepted_at.description: The parent 13F filing's SEC acceptance instant (UTC), joined from institutional_filing at export.

shares_or_principal_type.description: SH = shares | PRN = principal amount in dollars (then `shares` holds the face amount as filed, not a share count).  Filter `shares_or_principal_type = 'SH'` before summing shares.

other_managers.description: Sequence numbers this line cites from the filing's 'Other Included Managers' list (institutional_other_manager, list_kind = 'included'), normalised '1,2,4'.  NULL = none.

holding_line_no.description: The filing's own line sequence, 1-based.  (accession_id, holding_line_no) identifies the row.  NULL on older rows whose line order was not kept.

is_amendment.description: DERIVED: the parent filing is a 13F-HR/A.

superseded_by.description: DERIVED: accession of the 13F-HR/A RESTATEMENT that replaces this row's filing; NULL when current.

superseded_at.description: DERIVED: the accepted_at of the superseding restatement.  A book as of D is the rows with accepted_at <= D AND (superseded_at IS NULL OR superseded_at > D).

insider_ownership.description: SC 13D / SC 13G beneficial-ownership disclosures (5%+ stakes).  One row per (filing, reporting person).  Group filings carry multiple reporting persons — each lands as a separate row.  Joins to ``insider_filing`` via accession_id; subject_entity_id is the issuer CIK (the company being held — soft ref, LEFT JOIN to entity).  FULL bucket only — enterprise tier (full plan).

filer_cik.description: Reporting-person CIK; NULL when not SEC-registered (many institutional disclosures only carry a name).

filer_party_id.description: Link into `insider_party` for the reporting person.  Use it for cross-filing roll-ups (every disclosure by this filer over time); `filer_name` stays as the verbatim cover-page text for display.

subject_entity_id.description: Issuer CIK — the company whose stock is held.  Soft reference — LEFT JOIN to entity.cik when in the fundamentals universe.

schedule_type.description: SC 13D | SC 13D/A | SC 13G | SC 13G/A (or SCHEDULE 13… long-form variants — both vocabularies accepted).

accepted_at.description: The parent filing's SEC acceptance instant (UTC), joined from insider_filing at export.

superseded_by.description: Accession of the SAME reporting person's next SC 13D/G on the same subject (original or amendment, either schedule, in (accepted_at, accession_id) order); NULL on that person's latest filing.  Use this grain for positions: a group filing that drops a member leaves that member's last row current until the member files again.

reporting_person_type.description: Cover 'Type of Reporting Person' codes as filed (BD, BK, IC, IV, IA, EP, HC, SA, CP, CO, PN, IN, FI, OO); multi-valued.

is_amendment.description: DERIVED: the parent filing is an SC 13D/A or 13G/A.

superseded_at.description: DERIVED: the accepted_at of the superseded_by filing; NULL while current.

insider_footnote.description: Form 3 / 4 / 5 footnotes: the receipt behind a 10b5-1 plan, a weighted-average price or a plan adoption date.  Lines cite them through `insider_transaction.footnote_refs`.  Joins to `insider_filing` via accession_id.  Institutional (full) tier only; monolithic parquet only (no per-CIK partitions).

footnote_text.description: Verbatim footnote text; security identifiers redacted.

is_truncated.description: TRUE when the source capped the text.

accepted_at.description: DERIVED: the parent filing's SEC acceptance instant (UTC).

superseded_at.description: DERIVED: the accepted_at of the amendment that replaces the parent filing; NULL while current.

institutional_other_manager.description: 13F manager lists.  list_kind 'included' = the summary page's 'List of Other Included Managers' (numbered; cited by `institutional_holding.other_managers`); 'reporting_for' = the cover page's 'Other Managers Reporting for this Manager'.  Joins to `institutional_filing` via accession_id.  Institutional (full) tier only; monolithic parquet only.

ordinal.description: 1-based position in the list as filed.

name.description: Manager name as filed; security identifiers redacted.

accepted_at.description: DERIVED: the parent filing's SEC acceptance instant (UTC).

superseded_at.description: DERIVED: the accepted_at of the restatement that replaces the parent filing; NULL while current.

insider_ownership_purpose.description: Schedule 13D Item 4 'Purpose of Transaction', verbatim: raw filed text only, no summary and no classification.  13D / 13D/A only (13G has no Item 4); an amendment that does not restate Item 4 has NO row (never carried forward).  Joins to ``insider_filing`` via accession_id.  FULL bucket only; monolithic parquet only.

subject_cik.description: Issuer CIK whose shares the 13D concerns.

purpose_text.description: Whitespace-normalised Item 4 text, capped in length; security identifiers redacted.

char_count.description: Length of the full item before any cap.

is_truncated.description: TRUE when char_count exceeds the published text.

accepted_at.description: DERIVED: the parent filing's SEC acceptance instant (UTC).

superseded_at.description: DERIVED: the accepted_at of the filing that replaces the parent; NULL while current.

investment_adviser.description: SEC Form ADV Part 1A: registered investment advisers and Exempt Reporting Advisers (about 23.6K firms).  A separate SEC source from EDGAR: advisers file into IARD, so rows key on the firm's CRD number, not a CIK.  Point-in-time: the natural key is (crd_number, filing_date), where filing_date is the adviser's own Form ADV filing date.  A firm's annual updating amendment appends a new vintage instead of overwriting the prior one.  Filter `filing_date <= as_of` and take the latest vintage per crd_number for a point-in-time view, or the whole partition for adviser history.  Caveat: Items 5.A-5.F are absent for firm_type='ERA'.  Exempt Reporting Advisers file an abbreviated form; that is a different filing obligation, not missing data.  Scope coverage metrics to firm_type='Registered' or you understate completeness.  Institutional (full) tier only.

crd_number.description: IARD firm identifier (Item 1.E.(1)) — the natural key. Not a CIK.

filing_date.description: PIT vintage — the date the adviser filed this Form ADV.

sec_region.description: SEC regional office code, e.g. NYRO.

umbrella_registration.description: Filing covers a group of relying advisers under one umbrella registration.

cik.description: Soft link to EDGAR that the adviser disclosed itself (Item 1.D.(3)).  NULL for most advisers, so a NULL is expected, not an error.  Even where populated it rarely resolves to `entity`: most disclosed CIKs belong to SEC filers with no public ticker (broker-dealer subsidiaries, holding entities).  A real but rare bridge from an adviser to entity / institutional_holding, not a guaranteed one.

firm_type.description: 'Registered' (SEC-registered adviser) | 'ERA' (Exempt Reporting Adviser). ERAs file an abbreviated Form ADV — Items 5.A–5.F are NULL for them.

feed_generated_on.description: Date of the source snapshot this row came from (data freshness).

employees_advisory_research.description: Item 5.B.(1) — employees who perform investment advisory functions INCLUDING RESEARCH.  The in-house research-capacity measure; NULL for ERAs.

employees_registered_reps.description: Item 5.B.(2) — registered representatives of a broker-dealer.

clients_without_raum.description: Item 5.C.(1) — clients for whom the adviser reports NO regulatory AUM.

pct_clients_non_us.description: Item 5.C.(2) — percent of clients who are non-US persons (0-100).

client_type_counts.description: Item 5.D client counts keyed by category: individuals, hnw_individuals, banking_thrift, investment_companies, business_development_companies, pooled_investment_vehicles, pension_profit_sharing, charitable_organizations, government_entities, other_investment_advisers, insurance_companies, sovereign_wealth_funds, corporations, other.  Absent key = not reported.

client_type_raum.description: Item 5.D regulatory AUM by the same category keys as client_type_counts.  These values sum to raum_total for advisers reporting both.

reports_raum.description: Item 5.F.(1) — does the adviser report RAUM.

raum_total.description: Item 5.F.(2)(c): total regulatory assets under management (USD). WARNING: double-counted across sub-advisory and affiliated-adviser relationships, because the same dollars are reported by every adviser in the chain, so summing across firms gives a total far above real AUM.  Valid per firm and for ranking or screening; never aggregate it.

advisory_activities.description: Item 5.G.(1)-(12) service-type booleans: financial_planning, portfolio_mgmt_individuals, portfolio_mgmt_investment_companies, portfolio_mgmt_pooled_vehicles, portfolio_mgmt_businesses, pension_consulting, selection_of_other_advisers, publication_of_periodicals, security_ratings_or_pricing, market_timing_services, educational_seminars, other.

financial_planning_clients.description: Item 5.H: financial-planning client count, published by the SEC as a bucket string ('0', '1-10', '11-25', '26-50', '51-100', '101-250', '251-500', 'More than 500'), not an integer.  Do not cast to a number.

affiliations.description: Item 7.A.(1)-(16) financial-industry affiliation booleans: broker_dealer, registered_rep_of_broker_dealer, commodity_pool_operator_or_cta, futures_commission_merchant, real_estate_broker_or_agent, insurance_company_or_agency, pension_consultant, trust_company, registered_municipal_advisor, registered_sb_swap_dealer, major_sb_swap_participant, accountant_or_accounting_firm, lawyer_or_law_firm, banking_or_thrift_institution, sponsor_or_syndicator_of_lps, other_investment_adviser_or_financial_planner.

has_private_funds.description: Item 7.B flag: does the adviser advise any private fund.  Fund-level detail lives in `investment_adviser_private_fund`; a TRUE here with no child rows means that adviser's fund detail is not loaded yet, not that it does not exist.

source.description: Provenance label of the source feed.

investment_adviser_private_fund.description: Form ADV Schedule D, Section 7.B.(1): private funds advised by a registered investment adviser.  One row per (adviser, fund, filing vintage); joins to `investment_adviser` on crd_number.  Coverage caveat: fund detail arrives as advisers file their annual updating amendment, so coverage builds up over a year and can be partial.  A partial load looks complete but is not: use `investment_adviser.has_private_funds` for the authoritative population.  Institutional (full) tier only.

crd_number.description: Advising firm's CRD number (soft ref — the parent is vintage-keyed).

fund_id.description: SEC private-fund identifier, e.g. '805-4964869201'. Stable across filings.

filing_date.description: PIT vintage — filing date of the reporting ADV.

filing_id.description: IARD FilingID the row was parsed from.

reference_id.description: Per-filing fund sequence id; join key to the Schedule D sub-files.

fund_type.description: Hedge Fund | Private Equity Fund | Real Estate Fund | Venture Capital Fund | Liquidity Fund | Securitized Asset Fund | Other Private Fund.

gross_asset_value.description: Fund gross asset value in USD (Schedule D 7.B.(1)(A)(11)).  Unlike the adviser RAUM column this is fund-level and NOT double-counted across advisers, except for master/feeder pairs — filter is_feeder_fund to avoid counting a feeder's assets alongside its master's.

exclusion_3c1.description: Relies on the Investment Company Act §3(c)(1) exclusion (≤100 holders).

exclusion_3c7.description: Relies on the §3(c)(7) exclusion (qualified purchasers only).

is_feeder_fund.description: TRUE = feeder in a master-feeder structure; exclude when summing GAV.

has_annual_audit.description: Fund is subject to an annual audit.

is_gaap.description: Financial statements prepared under US GAAP.

unqualified_opinion.description: Most recent audit produced an unqualified opinion.

uses_prime_broker.description: Fund uses a prime broker.  A PRESENCE flag — the SEC reports Y/N here, not a name.

auditor_name.description: Auditing firm name, resolved from Schedule D 7.B.(1)(A)(23).

auditor_pcaob_registered.description: Auditor is registered with the PCAOB (7.B.(1)(A)(23)).

source.description: Provenance label of the source file.

corporate_action.description: Corporate actions read from SEC filings: name and ticker changes, delistings, bankruptcies, completed mergers (target side), splits, cash dividends and spin-offs.  One row per event.  `cik` is the company the event happened to (a spin-off sits on the parent; `child_cik` links the child).  Point-in-time: filter `first_known_at <= as_of` (the SEC acceptance time of the evidence filing).  `event_date` is the one date to window on.  Rows whose accuracy is below our precision bar are published with `is_uncertain` = TRUE and a 0-1 `confidence`.  `evidence_text` and `accession_id` let a reader check any row against the filing.  SEC-only: no vendor data, no CUSIP/CINS/ISIN.

cik.description: The company the event happened to (10-digit CIK); the PARENT for a spin-off.

action_type.description: name_change | ticker_change | delisting | bankruptcy | merger_completed | split | cash_dividend | spin_off.

action_subtype.description: forward_split / reverse_split, regular / special, bankruptcy stage, delisting scope, merger consideration (target_completed_cash / _stock / _stock_and_cash), and similar.

security_class.description: Share class as filed (Common Stock, Series B Preferred); NULL when the filing does not name it (the row is then per company).

event_date.description: Effective date, else ex-date, payable, record or declared date, else the evidence filing's date. The rolling-window column.

effective_date.description: Effective date (split, merger, bankruptcy stage, name change), when stated.

ex_date.description: Ex-dividend date: stated, or derived (see ex_date_basis).

declared_date_source.description: Dividends: board (the filing says the board declared on that date) or release (the date of the press release or 8-K); NULL otherwise.

ex_date_basis.description: stated, or derived_t1 / derived_t2 ...; NULL when there is no ex-date.

date_precision.description: day or month when the filing gave less than a full date; NULL means day.

ratio_new.description: Splits: shares after per ratio_old before. Spin-offs: child shares per ratio_old parent shares. Mergers: acquirer shares received per ratio_old (1) target share.

amount.description: Cash dividends: cash per share. Mergers: cash paid per target share. In currency.

currency.description: ISO currency of amount (USD unless the filing says otherwise).

old_value.description: Name or ticker before the change.

new_value.description: Name or ticker after the change.

counterparty.description: Acquirer (merger) or spin-off child, as named in the filing.

child_cik.description: Spin-offs: the child's CIK when the child's name resolves to exactly one entity; NULL otherwise.

first_known_at.description: PIT clock: SEC acceptance time of the earliest filing that states the event. Never the load time.

accession_id.description: Evidence filing (the one first_known_at comes from).

form_type.description: Form type of the evidence filing.

source_item.description: 8-K item of the evidence, when the form has items.

corroborated_by.description: Other accessions (or key names) that independently state the event.

method.description: Identifier of the rule that read the row from the filing.

extractor_version.description: Version of the reading rules that produced the row.

evidence_text.description: The filing sentence the row was read from (at most 400 characters, identifiers removed).

evidence_element.description: XBRL element the value was keyed to, when one was used; NULL for prose-only rows.

confidence.description: 0-1 share of graded rows of this kind that were right (event, company and every stated value).  NULL when not measured yet; such rows are is_uncertain.

is_uncertain.description: TRUE when confidence is below our precision bar or NULL (not measured).

fact_quarterly.description: Discrete quarters: one row per company, concept, fiscal year, quarter and filing: Q1-Q4 of every fiscal year, with the 10-K year split into Q4, for TTM sums and seasonality.  Every filing that carries a quarter keeps its own row (point in time); `is_latest` marks the most recently accepted version of each quarter.  Flows carry the discrete-quarter value; balance-sheet rows carry the quarter-end value as filed.  `fiscal_quarter` follows the company's own fiscal calendar, not the `fiscal_period` label.  A quarter the filings do not support is absent, not estimated: EPS and other per-share or share-count flows have no Q4.

fact_id.description: The source `fact` row's fact_id: the lineage key to its filing.

fiscal_year.description: Fiscal year of the quarter (the year of the company's fiscal close), as in `fact`.

fiscal_quarter.description: 1-4, the quarter's position in the company's fiscal year.

period_start.description: First day of the quarter: the filer's own start for `method = 'reported'`; for a derived quarter the day after the previous quarter ended, NULL when unknown.  NULL for `instant`.

period_end.description: Last day of the quarter (the balance date for `instant`).

value.description: The discrete-quarter value (flows) or the quarter-end value (instants).

method.description: How `value` was obtained: 'reported' (the filer printed the 3-month figure), 'ytd_subtraction' (a year-to-date total minus the prior one), 'fy_minus_9m' or 'fy_minus_quarters' (a Q4 derived from the fiscal year), 'instant' (a balance-sheet value at the quarter end).

is_uncertain.description: TRUE when the derivation was flagged (`fact.derivation_uncertain`): a prior year-to-date that does not reconcile, or a negative result for a concept that cannot be negative.  Always FALSE for 'reported' and 'instant'.

is_latest.description: TRUE on the most recently accepted version of this (entity_id, standard_concept, fiscal_year, fiscal_quarter); FALSE on earlier ones.  Filter `is_latest` for the current value, or `accepted_at <= T` for a point-in-time view.

data_quality.description: `fact.data_quality` of the source row ('standard' = XBRL-tagged by the filer).

price_daily.description: Daily prices of stocks, ETFs and funds from free public sources, as traded (unadjusted): one row per SEC registrant (`entity_id`), ticker (`symbol`) and trading day (`price_date`).  For an ETF or fund `entity_id` is the trust that files for it (one trust can hold many ETFs, so join on `symbol` too).  Every close is graded A, B or C; filter `close_grade IN ('A','B')` for backtests.  Coverage: IEX last sales for 2016-12-12 and from 2023-10-23 to 2026-11-11 (a few days missing; every other day is SEC-only) and SEC Fails-to-Deliver closes from 2007-04 (a security appears on days it had fails); a row's company is the one SEC's own dated ticker evidence says held the ticker that day, and a ticker-day that evidence contradicts or leaves ambiguous is left out, never guessed; OTC names are sparse and the table does not claim to be survivorship-free.  A split is never adjusted for: `split_suspect` only flags it.  Use `known_at` for point-in-time work: a close is not known before that date.  Data provided for free by IEX. By accessing or using IEX Historical Data, you agree to the IEX Historical Data Terms of Use. Terms: https://www.iex.io/legal/hist-data-terms  IEX data is a reference point and not a basis for trading decisions.  Prices taken from SEC Fails-to-Deliver files are as reported to the SEC; the SEC does not guarantee the accuracy of the Fails-to-Deliver data.

symbol.description: Ticker the price was reported under on `price_date`; tickers are reused, join on `entity_id`.

price_date.description: The trading day the prices describe.

open.description: Opening price, as traded.  NULL unless `open_grade` is 'A' or 'B'.

high.description: Day high, as traded.  NULL unless `high_grade` is 'A' or 'B'.

low.description: Day low, as traded.  NULL unless `low_grade` is 'A' or 'B'.

close.description: Closing price, as traded (unadjusted for splits and dividends).  Always positive.

close_source.description: 'iex_last_sale' = the last regular-session sale on IEX (not the consolidated official close); 'sec_ftd' = the prior-day closing price the SEC prints in its Fails-to-Deliver files.

close_grade.description: A = calibrated: 98%+ of days within 0.5% of the official close; B = 95%+ within 2%; C = neither.  Filter `close_grade IN ('A','B')` for backtests.

open_grade.description: 'A' or 'B' (same scale as `close_grade`); NULL when `open` is NULL.

high_grade.description: 'A' or 'B' (same scale as `close_grade`); NULL when `high` is NULL.

low_grade.description: 'A' or 'B' (same scale as `close_grade`); NULL when `low` is NULL.

known_at.description: Date the source file carrying this close was published: the next trading day for IEX, the file's own date for SEC Fails-to-Deliver (typically 2-6 weeks after `price_date`).  Filter `known_at <= T` for a point-in-time view.

split_suspect.description: TRUE when the ratio of this close to the previous one is near a split factor.  A flag only: prices are never adjusted.
